# Adjudication Task — Chapter 547

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃547화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|대회의실에 싸늘한 침묵이 내려앉았다.
  6|
  7|사실 말을 꺼내기 전에도 충분히 예상했던 반응이다.
  8|
  9|그리고 이 자리에 있는 수십여 명의 사람들 중, 누가 가장 먼저 나를 향해 날 선 말을 내뱉을지도.
 10|
 11|“그걸, 지금 말이라고 하나?”
 12|
 13|어떻게 예상을 벗어나는 법이 없냐.
 14|
 15|나는 기다렸다는 듯이 입을 연 반백의 중년인을 보며 내심 혀를 찼다.
 16|
 17|저 사람의 이름과 신분은 이미 들어서 알고 있다. 지난번 회동 때부터 하도 째려보길래 뭐 하는 인간인가, 했더니 역시나 간접적인 인연이 있었거든.
 18|
 19|‘씨는 못 속인다더니.’
 20|
 21|확실히 부자지간이라 그런지 닮긴 닮았다. 날카롭게 솟구친 눈매도, 사람을 깔보는 오만한 눈빛과 말투도.
 22|
 23|“내 말이 안 들리는 모양이군.”
 24|
 25|반백의 중년인. 산동권룡(山東拳龍) 황보악의 아버지이자 황보세가의 가주인 황보군의 물음에, 나는 천천히 눈을 깜빡였다.
 26|
 27|“당연히 들리죠. 설마 안 들리겠습니까?”
 28|
 29|“그런데 왜 대답이 없지?”
 30|
 31|“질문이 웃기잖아요. 제 입으로 한 말이니까 당연히 말이라고 생각해서 한 거지. 제가 뭐 짐승처럼 울음소리라도 냈어요?”
 32|
 33|옆자리에 앉은 청풍이 귀를 쫑긋 세웠다.
 34|
 35|“은인, 그런 소리도 낼 수 있어요?”
 36|
 37|“청 소협은 입 다물고 있어. 배 속에 있는 만두 토해 내기 싫으면.”
 38|
 39|“고마워요…….”
 40|
 41|이를 지켜보는 황보군의 표정이 와락 구겨졌다.
 42|
 43|“이 자리가 어떤 자리인 줄 모르느냐!”
 44|
 45|“그거 모르고 온 사람 있습니까.”
 46|
 47|“한데 명성이 자자하신 노선배님들 앞에서, 그런 뻔한 말을 상스럽게 내뱉다니!”
 48|
 49|“그래서 말 안 하려고 했잖습니까. 그리고 이건 노선배님들 입장도 들어 봐야죠. 어떻게 생각하십니까?”
 50|
 51|갑작스러운 내 물음에 매종학이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 52|
 53|“그건 진 각주 말이 맞지. 나는 별 상관없네. 말이 험하긴 해도 현실을 직시해야지.”
 54|
 55|“매, 맹주님!”
 56|
 57|당황함이 가득 묻어 나오는 황보군의 외침을, 나는 잽싸게 가로챘다.
 58|
 59|“예. 바로 그 무림 맹주님의 고견, 잘 들었습니다. 내친김에 우리 오왕전주님께서는?”
 60|
 61|적천강이 벌레 보는 듯한 눈빛으로 황보군을 바라봤다.
 62|
 63|“뭘 묻고 자빠졌느냐. 좆 된 거 맞지. 저놈의 헛소리는 신경 쓸 것 없으니 계속해라.”
 64|
 65|“화끈한 대답 감사합니다.”
 66|
 67|고개를 돌려 황보군을 응시한 내가 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
 68|
 69|“그렇다는데요, 바로 그 노선배님들께서.”
 70|
 71|“……!”
 72|
 73|이 자리에 노선배라고 칭할 만한 사람들은 차고 넘치지만, 적천강과 매종학에 비견할 수 있는 자는 아무도 없다.
 74|
 75|구파일방과 오대세가의 주인들이 분대장을 맡은 실세 상병에 말년 병장이라면, 무림 맹주인 매종학은 대대장이요 적천강은 주임 원사인 것이다.
 76|
 77|‘짬에서 밀리면 입 다물어야지.’
 78|
 79|짬도 짬인데. 심지어 계급장 떼고 덤벼도 화왕표 불 주먹 한 방이면 훅 간다.
 80|
 81|이것이 나와 청풍을 곱게 보지 않는 이들, 그중에서도 대표 주자라 할 수 있는 종남파 장문인 풍운검군조차 입을 꾹 다물고 있는 이유였다.
 82|
 83|그리고 그건 황보군이 외톨이 신세가 되었다는 뜻이나 다름없었다.
 84|
 85|‘누울 자리를 보고 다리를 뻗지. 그러게 왜 혼자 나서서 저래.’
 86|
 87|황보군도 정마대전 때는 방귀깨나 뀌었다고 들었는데. 원래도 정치 감각이 떨어졌던 건지, 아니면 삼대독자 외아들에 관련된 일로 폭주 기관차가 된 건지 모르겠다.
 88|
 89|나는 안타까움을 담은 구슬픈 멜로디를 흥얼거렸다.
 90|
 91|“나는 개똥벌레. 친구가 없네.”
 92|
 93|“이, 이 어린놈이 감히!”
 94|
 95|여기서 끝낼 수는 없지. 나는 야무지게 준비해 둔 콤보를 꽂아 넣었다.
 96|
 97|“응애. 나 애기 각주.”
 98|
 99|“노오옴-!”
100|
101|쿠당탕!
102|
103|자리를 박차고 일어난 그의 불끈 쥔 주먹에 핏줄이 툭툭 불거진다.
104|
105|아무런 이득도, 본전도 찾지 못한 황보군이 분노에 가득 찬 눈으로 나를 노려보던 그 순간이었다.
106|
107|“놈이라……. 외람되지만 황보 가주께 한 가지만 여쭙겠습니다.”
108|
109|불현듯 들려온 한마디.
110|
111|부드러운 목소리 속엔 단단한 심지가 느껴졌다.
112|
113|어느새 황보군을 응시하는 진위경의 눈동자는 서늘하게 가라앉아 있었다.
114|
115|“묻건대, 황보 가주께서는 무림맹 내에서의 직책이 어찌 되십니까?”
116|
117|“……!”
118|
119|“아무리 화룡각주의 연배가 어리다 해도, 그는 화왕 적천강 대협의 진전을 이은 후인이자 무림맹의 각주입니다. 강호의 배분을 따져 보아도 결코 황보 가주의 아래가 아니지요.”
120|
121|정곡이다. 아픈 부분을 찔린 황보군의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
122|
123|그는 산동지방의 패자인 황보세가의 가주지만, 한 지방의 방비를 책임지는 외당 단주(團主)에 그쳤다.
124|
125|그러니 공식적인 무림맹 직책 서열상으로는 내당 각주인 내 아래라고 할 수 있었다.
126|
127|“그건…….”
128|
129|말을 잇지 못하고 입술을 질끈 깨문 황보군이 도움을 청할 곳을 찾아 주위를 둘러본다.
130|
131|하지만 그의 기대와는 달리, 황보군을 향한 사람들의 반응은 뜨뜻미지근했다.
132|
133|“아미타불. 이만 자중하는 게 어떻겠소, 황보 시주.”
134|
135|“허어, 신성한 맹주전에서 이런 소란이라니.”
136|
137|“열화신룡. 아니, 화룡각주의 편을 드는 것이 아닐세. 두 사람 다 그만하면 되었으니 이만 자리에 앉게.”
138|
139|내가 천연덕스럽게 대답했다.
140|
141|“저는 처음부터 자리에 앉아 있었습니다.”
142|
143|“그럼 한 사람만 남았군.”
144|
145|누구를 가리키는 말인지는 명백하다.
146|
147|그리고 이제는 멈춰야 한다는 이성적인 판단과 동한 지방의 패자이자 일가의 가주가 지닌 마지막 자존심 사이에서 갈등하던 황보군을 향해, 결정 장애를 해결할 수 있는 한마디가 날아들었다.
148|
149|“귓구녕에 암기라도 박았느냐?”
150|
151|화왕 적천강. 그의 짤막한 한마디와 함께 대회의실의 공기가 뜨겁게 달아오른다.
152|
153|붉은 안광이 감도는 두 눈동자에 얼어붙은 황보군의 모습이 비쳤다.
154|
155|“앉아. 지금 당장.”
156|
157|“……!”
158|
159|화아아악!
160|
161|허공을 격하며 덮쳐 오는 기세에, 황보군의 눈이 부릅떠졌다. 아니, 대회의실에 자리한 모두가 마찬가지였다.
162|
163|“으음.”
164|
165|말없이 상황을 지켜보던 권왕 언화평이 신음을 흘리고.
166|
167|“저, 적가. 네놈……!”
168|
169|벽력도왕 팽철후의 시선이 격동한다.
170|
171|그만큼 적천강의 기세는 강대했고, 또 하나의 태양처럼 압도적이었다.
172|
173|아직 절정의 경지에 머무르는 자도, 이미 초절정에 오른 이들도 그의 힘을 느낄 수 있었다.
174|
175|‘반로환동(返老還童).’
176|
177|무공이라는 이름의 산맥은 험난하며 광활하다. 때로는 가파른 협곡을 지나쳐야 하고 깎아내린 듯한 절벽을 올라야 한다.
178|
179|그리고 적천강은…… 그 끝에 존재하는 봉우리에 우뚝 선 위대한 무인이다.
180|
181|지금의 그는 화왕(火王)이라는 별호를 뛰어넘는 존재가 되어 있었다. 이 자리의 또 다른 한 사람과 함께.
182|
183|“적 대협.”
184|
185|검성 매종학의 나직한 목소리가 울려 퍼진 순간, 대회의실을 휩쓸던 열풍(熱風)이 사라졌다.
186|
187|순식간에 자신의 기세를 갈무리한 적천강이 퉁명스럽게 대꾸했다.
188|
189|“무슨 일 있었소?”
190|
191|“흠.”
192|
193|“알겠소. 알았다니까. 저놈이 너무 시끄럽게 굴기에 겁 좀 준 것뿐이오.”
194|
195|농담이 아니라, 두 번 겁줬다가는 오줌이라도 지릴 거다.
196|
197|적천강이 말하는 ‘그놈’은 이미 새하얗게 질린 얼굴로 자리에 앉아 있었으니까.
198|
199|“이제야 조용해졌군.”
200|
201|작게 중얼거리는 적천강을 부드럽게 질책하는 눈빛으로 바라본 매종학이 입술을 뗐다.
202|
203|어느덧 그의 시선은 나를 똑바로 향하고 있었다.
204|
205|“화룡각주.”
206|
207|“네.”
208|
209|“자네는 산서와 하남. 그리고 사천과 호북에서 암천의 흉계에 맞섰지.”
210|
211|정확히 말하자면 휘말렸다고 해야겠지만, 나는 조용히 고개를 끄덕였다.
212|
213|이곳은 무림맹의 대회의장. 황보군을 상대하는 것과 앞으로의 중대사를 논하는 것은 비교할 수 없는 차이가 있다.
214|
215|“그렇습니다.”
216|
217|“예상컨대 자네만큼 암천에 잘 아는 사람은 드물겠지. 하여 본 맹주는 자네의 고견(高見)을 묻고 싶네.”
218|
219|“저는 그 현장에 있었을 뿐. 확실한 정황과 천하 곳곳에서 무슨 일이 벌어지는지는 은영각에서 더 잘 알고 있을 겁니다. 이미 모든 것을 알려 드리기도 했고요.”
220|
221|“직접 보고 겪은 그대로를 원하네. 그 모든 상황을 겪은 자네가 속에 품은 생각을.”
222|
223|그래. 이렇게 나와야지.
224|
225|앞에 던진 말은 앞으로 해야 할 말을 위한 밑밥에 불과하다.
226|
227|한두 번의 양보와 사양은 미덕이고, 무림 맹주로서의 권위를 지닌 매종학이 이렇게까지 내 의견을 묻는다면 그만큼 힘이 실리기 마련이다.
228|
229|‘좋아.’
230|
231|나는 작게 심호흡했다.
232|
233|지금까지의 내 위치가 자동차 뒷좌석이었다면 지금부터는 조수석이다.
234|
235|짙은 안개가 낀 새벽, 내비게이션도 없이 초행길에 나선 운전자에게 내가 아는 모든 것을 알려 줄 수는 없다.
236|
237|그러나 과속방지턱이 어디에 있는지, 지금 달려가는 이 길 앞에 무엇이 기다리고 있는지 정도는 말해 줄 수 있을 것이다.
238|
239|‘얼마 전부터 머릿속을 떠나지 않던 그 불길한 생각도.’
240|
241|생각을 정리하고 고개를 들자, 대회의실의 모든 사람이 오직 나 한 사람만을 바라보고 있었다.
242|
243|수십 쌍의 시선.
244|
245|이미 시작된 전쟁에서 수백, 수천의 목숨을 살릴 수도. 죽일 수도 있는 이들이다.
246|
247|그들이 고작 약관을 넘긴 어린 핏덩이의 말을 얼마나 마음에 새길지는 미지수지만…….
248|
249|‘상관없다. 이 전쟁에서 승리할 수 있다면. 조금이라도 위험과 희생을 줄일 수 있다면.’
250|
251|지금 당장. 내가 할 수 있는 일을 해야 한다.
252|
253|그런 생각 때문일까. 다음 순간 내 입술 사이로 흘러나온 목소리에는 평소와 다른 힘이 실려 있었다.
254|
255|“암천은…….”
256|
257|
258|
259|* * *
260|
261|
262|
263|두 시진 뒤. 사람들이 모두 빠져나간 대회의실에는 단 세 사람만이 남아 있었다.
264|
265|조금 전까지만 하더라도 수십여 명의 사람들이 자리했던 의자는 텅 비어 있었지만, 어느 순간부터 내려앉은 침묵은 떠나지 않았다.
266|
267|아마 맹주전을 나간 이들 역시 지금쯤 그럴 것이라고, 천면호리 송호는 생각했다.
268|
269|‘그럴 만도 하지.’
270|
271|진태경의 입에서 흘러나온 말들은 그만큼 충격적이었다.
272|
273|암천의 존재와 위험성을 모르는 사람은 없었지만, 그 젊은 청년만큼 위기를 경고한 사람은 아무도 없었다.
274|
275|‘심지어 나조차도.’
276|
277|은영각은 천하 각지의 정보를 끌어모아 수많은 예측을 쏟아낸다.
278|

Jeok Cheongang looked at Hwangbo Gun as though he were a bug.

[P30]
“Why the hell are you asking? We’re fucked. Ignore that bastard’s nonsense and keep going.”

[P31]
“Thank you for the fiery answer.”

[P32]
I turned to Hwangbo Gun and shrugged.

[P33]
“That’s what those esteemed Seniors have to say.”

[P34]
“……!”

[P35]
There were plenty of people here who could be called Seniors, but none of them could compare to Jeok Cheongang and Mae Jonghak.

[P36]
If the heads of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were squad-leading corporals with pull or sergeants nearing discharge, Murim Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak was the battalion commander, and Jeok Cheongang was the command sergeant major.

[P37]
*If you don’t have the seniority, keep your mouth shut.*

[P38]
And it wasn’t just seniority. Strip off the insignia and take Jeok Cheongang on as an equal, and one punch from the Fire King would lay you out.

[P39]
That was why even the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect and one of the foremost among those who disliked Cheongpung and me, kept his mouth firmly shut.

[P40]
Which left Hwangbo Gun all alone.

[P41]
*You should’ve looked before stretching out your legs. Why step forward on your own?*

[P42]
I’d heard Hwangbo Gun wielded considerable influence during the Great Faction War. Maybe he’d always lacked political sense. Or maybe a matter involving his only son—the sole heir in three generations—had turned him into a runaway locomotive.

[P43]
I hummed a mournful tune.

[P44]
“I’m a firefly. I have no friends.”

[P45]
“You insolent young punk!”

[P46]
I couldn’t stop there. I hit him with the combo I’d prepared.

[P47]
“Waaah. I’m a baby Pavilion Master.”

[P48]
“You braaaat!”

[P49]
*Crash!*

[P50]
Hwangbo Gun sprang to his feet, veins standing out on his clenched fists. He glared at me, furious and empty-handed, without so much as breaking even.

[P51]
Then a voice spoke.

[P52]
“‘Punk,’ you say… Forgive me, Family Head Hwangbo, but may I ask you one question?”

[P53]
The voice was gentle, with a firmness beneath it. Jin Wikyung’s eyes had gone cold as he looked at Hwangbo Gun.

[P54]
“What position do you hold within the Murim Alliance, Family Head Hwangbo?”

[P55]
“……!”

[P56]
“The Fire Dragon Pavilion Master may be young, but he has inherited the martial legacy of Great Hero Jeok, the Fire King, and he is a Pavilion Master of the Murim Alliance. Even by the martial world’s rules of seniority, he is certainly not beneath you.”

[P57]
That hit the sore spot. Hwangbo Gun’s face stiffened.

[P58]
He was Family Head of the Hwangbo Family, the hegemon of Shandong, but within the Alliance he was only an Outer Hall Squad Leader charged with defending one region.

[P59]
In the Murim Alliance’s official hierarchy, that put him below me, an Inner Hall Pavilion Master.

[P60]
“That…”

[P61]
Unable to continue, Hwangbo Gun bit his lip and looked around for help.

[P62]
The response was lukewarm.

[P63]
“Amitabha. Perhaps it would be best to restrain yourself now, Benefactor Hwangbo.”

[P64]
“Heavens. Such a disturbance in the sacred Alliance Leader’s Hall.”

[P65]
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—no, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. I’m not taking your side. Both of you have said enough. Sit down.”

[P66]
I answered without a hint of shame.

[P67]
“I’ve been sitting down the whole time.”

[P68]
“Then there’s only one person left.”

[P69]
It was obvious whom he meant.

[P70]
Hwangbo Gun was caught between the good sense telling him to stop and the last shred of pride he had as Shandong’s hegemon and the head of his family.

[P71]
One remark settled his indecision.

[P72]
“Got a hidden weapon stuck in your ear?”

[P73]
It came from the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. The air in the hall heated with those few words.

[P74]
Hwangbo Gun stood frozen, reflected in Jeok Cheongang’s red-glowing eyes.

[P75]
“Sit down. Right now.”

[P76]
“……!”

[P77]
*Whoooosh!*

[P78]
Jeok Cheongang’s aura surged through the air and crashed over them. Hwangbo Gun’s eyes flew wide.

[P79]
So did everyone else’s.

[P80]
“Hmm.”

[P81]
Fist King Yan Hwapyeong, who had watched in silence, let out a low groan.

[P82]
“J-Jeok! You bastard…!”

[P83]
The Thunderbolt Saber King Peng Cheolhu’s gaze wavered.

[P84]
Jeok Cheongang’s aura was that powerful, that overwhelming—like another sun. Those still in the Peak realm could feel his strength, as could those who had already reached Supreme Peak.

[P85]
*Returned to Youth.*

[P86]
The mountain range called martial arts was vast and treacherous. Sometimes one had to cross a steep ravine or scale a sheer cliff.

[P87]
And Jeok Cheongang stood atop the peak at its farthest end.

[P88]
He had become something beyond his title of Fire King. So had one other person in this room.

[P89]
“Great Hero Jeok.”

[P90]
At Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s quiet call, the hot wind sweeping through the hall vanished.

[P91]
Jeok Cheongang drew in his aura at once and answered gruffly.

[P92]
“Did something happen?”

[P93]
“Hmm.”

[P94]
“All right, I know. That bastard was making too much noise, so I gave him a little scare.”

[P95]
No joke—if he scared Hwangbo Gun a second time, the man might wet himself. He was already back in his seat, white as a sheet.

[P96]
“Finally, some quiet,” Jeok Cheongang muttered.

[P97]
Mae Jonghak gave him a gently reproachful look, then turned to me.

[P98]
“Fire Dragon Pavilion Master.”

[P99]
“Yes.”

[P100]
“You have stood against Dark Heaven in Shanxi and Henan, and in Sichuan and Hubei.”

[P101]
*Gotten dragged into it* would have been more accurate, but I nodded.

[P102]
This was the Murim Alliance’s great conference hall. Sparring with Hwangbo Gun was one thing; discussing what came next was another.

[P103]
“That’s right.”

[P104]
“I expect few people know Dark Heaven as well as you. I would like to hear your opinion.”

[P105]
“I was only there when those things happened. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion knows more about the concrete evidence and what’s happening across the realm. I’ve already told them everything I know.”

[P106]
“I want to hear what you saw and experienced yourself. What the man who went through it all truly thinks.”

[P107]
*There we go.*

[P108]
What I’d said before was only a lead-in. Demurring once or twice was the polite thing to do, and if Mae Jonghak, speaking with the authority of the Murim Alliance Leader, pressed me for my opinion, it would carry that much more weight.

[P109]
*All right.*

[P110]
I took a small breath.

[P111]
Until now, I’d been sitting in the back seat. From here on, I was in the passenger seat.

[P112]
I couldn’t tell a driver setting out on an unfamiliar road at dawn, through thick fog and without navigation, everything I knew. But I could point out the speed bumps and warn him what lay ahead.

[P113]
*Including the ominous thought I haven’t been able to shake lately.*

[P114]
I sorted through my thoughts and raised my head. Everyone in the hall was looking at me.

[P115]
Dozens of pairs of eyes.

[P116]
These people could save hundreds, even thousands of lives in the war that had already begun. Or they could get them killed.

[P117]
How much heed they would pay to a kid barely past twenty, I couldn’t say.

[P118]
*It doesn’t matter. If we can win this war—if I can reduce the danger and the losses even a little—*

[P119]
I had to do what I could. Right now.

[P120]
Perhaps that was why my voice carried a weight it usually didn’t when I began to speak.

[P121]
“Dark Heaven…”

[P122]
* * *

[P123]
Two shichen later,[^1] everyone had left the great conference hall except three people.

[P124]
The chairs that had held dozens of people stood empty, but the silence that had settled over the room remained. Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho suspected those who had left the Alliance Leader’s Hall were just as quiet.

[P125]
*They had every reason to be.*

[P126]
Jin Taekyung’s words had been that shocking.

[P127]
Everyone knew Dark Heaven existed and understood that it was dangerous. No one, though, had warned of the coming crisis as forcefully as that young man.

[P128]
*Not even me.*

[P129]
The Hidden Shadow Pavilion gathered intelligence from across the realm and issued countless predictions. Hundreds of messenger pigeons arrived each day with information tied to their slender ankles, then flew off again before long.

[P130]
As its chief, Song Ho knew how dangerous Dark Heaven was.

[P131]
*But…*

[P132]
The thinking of the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s young master, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon whose actions had caused one upheaval after another, went far beyond anything Song Ho had expected.

[P133]
Where others spoke of danger, Jin Taekyung foretold disaster. When someone cited the Great Faction War as grounds for believing the Murim Alliance would win, he answered sharply.

[P134]
“Are we fighting the Demonic Cult? Our opponent is Dark Heaven. Dark Heaven.”

[P135]
“What Dark Heaven has shown us isn’t simply demonic martial arts. So what do I call it? Ah, this is driving me crazy. Fine. Let’s call it demonic martial arts for now.”

[P136]
“I don’t know why Dark Heaven has gone quiet, but we need to use this opening to strike back immediately. If we keep going like this, we’re finished. Everyone dies.”

[P137]
“Who said I was going too far? You, Family Head. Have you ever fought someone who came back to life even after all four limbs were crushed? Or fought an imugi? When you saw that monster half an hour ago, was all you could think about what to eat for dinner?”

[P138]
“We aren’t fighting ordinary people. Dark Heaven is one enormous monster, and before long, we may have to fight monsters like that one.”

[P139]
“I went a little too far. But this needs saying: we have to take every measure we can, right now. Especially if you’ve got a divine artifact at home that you guard like an ancestral shrine.”

[P140]
Song Ho suddenly furrowed his brow.

[P141]
The place where his prosthetic leg attached had begun to throb when Jin Taekyung started speaking. Now it burned.

[P142]
*It wasn’t like this even a year ago.*

[P143]
The pain had returned at some point and begun tormenting him in his old age, as though warning him this was no time to sit still.

[P144]
And today, that young man was here too.

[P145]
*It was as though he knew. As though he’d already experienced something and could foresee a truth hidden from me and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion—no, from everyone else.*

[P146]
Foresee? No. Song Ho corrected himself.

[P147]
*It was more like a prophecy.*

[P148]
The question was whether it truly was one.

[P149]
Could he trust the young man who, more than anyone else in the realm, had come into contact with Dark Heaven? How much of what he’d said was truth, and how much was exaggeration?

[P150]
“Believe him.”

[P151]
“Hm?”

[P152]
Song Ho looked up sharply. Jeok Cheongang, still in the hall, continued.

[P153]
“I said, believe him.”

[P154]
“Great Hero Jeok.”

[P155]
“I know what you’re going to say. But…”

[P156]
His tone softened.

[P157]
“The kid I know has never once been wrong.”

[P158]
“……!”

[P159]
Song Ho faltered at the absolute trust in those words.

[P160]
Then Mae Jonghak, the last of the three remaining in the hall, spoke.

[P161]
“There are certainties in this world that information alone cannot lead us to.”

[P162]
“Alliance Leader. Do you mean…?”

[P163]
“That’s right.”

[P164]
Mae Jonghak rose slowly from his seat.

[P165]
“Summon him. It’s time to give the Fire Dragon Pavilion its first mission.”

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Thank you for the fiery answer.”

[P32]
I turned to Hwangbo Gun and shrugged.

[P33]
“That’s what those esteemed Seniors have to say.”

[P34]
“……!”

[P35]
There were plenty of people here who could be called Seniors, but none of them could compare to Jeok Cheongang and Mae Jonghak.

[P36]
If the heads of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were squad-leading corporals with pull or sergeants nearing discharge, Murim Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak was the battalion commander, and Jeok Cheongang was the command sergeant major.

[P37]
*If you don’t have the seniority, keep your mouth shut.*

[P38]
And it wasn’t just seniority. Strip off the insignia and take Jeok Cheongang on as an equal, and one punch from the Fire King would lay you out.

[P39]
That was why even the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect and one of the foremost among those who disliked Cheongpung and me, kept his mouth firmly shut.

[P40]
Which left Hwangbo Gun all alone.

[P41]
*You should’ve looked before stretching out your legs. Why step forward on your own?*

[P42]
I’d heard Hwangbo Gun wielded considerable influence during the Great Faction War. Maybe he’d always lacked political sense. Or maybe a matter involving his only son—the sole heir in three generations—had turned him into a runaway locomotive.

[P43]
I hummed a mournful tune.

[P44]
“I’m a firefly. I have no friends.”

[P45]
“You insolent young punk!”

[P46]
I couldn’t stop there. I hit him with the combo I’d prepared.

[P47]
“Waaah. I’m a baby Pavilion Master.”

[P48]
“You braaaat!”

[P49]
*Crash!*

[P50]
Hwangbo Gun sprang to his feet, veins standing out on his clenched fists. He glared at me, furious and empty-handed, without so much as breaking even.

[P51]
Then a voice spoke.

[P52]
“‘Punk,’ you say… Forgive me, Family Head Hwangbo, but may I ask you one question?”

[P53]
The voice was gentle, with a firmness beneath it. Jin Wikyung’s eyes had gone cold as he looked at Hwangbo Gun.

[P54]
“What position do you hold within the Murim Alliance, Family Head Hwangbo?”

[P55]
“……!”

[P56]
“The Fire Dragon Pavilion Master may be young, but he has inherited the martial legacy of Great Hero Jeok, the Fire King, and he is a Pavilion Master of the Murim Alliance. Even by the martial world’s rules of seniority, he is certainly not beneath you.”

[P57]
That hit the sore spot. Hwangbo Gun’s face stiffened.

[P58]
He was Family Head of the Hwangbo Family, the hegemon of Shandong, but within the Alliance he was only an Outer Hall Squad Leader charged with defending one region.

[P59]
In the Murim Alliance’s official hierarchy, that put him below me, an Inner Hall Pavilion Master.

[P60]
“That…”

[P61]
Unable to continue, Hwangbo Gun bit his lip and looked around for help.

[P62]
The response was lukewarm.

[P63]
“Amitabha. Perhaps it would be best to restrain yourself now, Benefactor Hwangbo.”

[P64]
“Heavens. Such a disturbance in the sacred Alliance Leader’s Hall.”

[P65]
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—no, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. I’m not taking your side. Both of you have said enough. Sit down.”

[P66]
I answered without a hint of shame.

[P67]
“I’ve been sitting down the whole time.”

[P68]
“Then there’s only one person left.”

[P69]
It was obvious whom he meant.

[P70]
Hwangbo Gun was caught between the good sense telling him to stop and the last shred of pride he had as Shandong’s hegemon and the head of his family.

[P71]
One remark settled his indecision.

[P72]
“Got a hidden weapon stuck in your ear?”

[P73]
It came from the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. The air in the hall heated with those few words.

[P74]
Hwangbo Gun stood frozen, reflected in Jeok Cheongang’s red-glowing eyes.

[P75]
“Sit down. Right now.”

[P76]
“……!”

[P77]
*Whoooosh!*

[P78]
Jeok Cheongang’s aura surged through the air and crashed over them. Hwangbo Gun’s eyes flew wide.

[P79]
So did everyone else’s.

[P80]
“Hmm.”

[P81]
Fist King Yan Hwapyeong, who had watched in silence, let out a low groan.

[P82]
“J-Jeok! You bastard…!”

[P83]
The Thunderbolt Saber King Peng Cheolhu’s gaze wavered.

[P84]
Jeok Cheongang’s aura was that powerful, that overwhelming—like another sun. Those still in the Peak realm could feel his strength, as could those who had already reached Supreme Peak.

[P85]
*Returned to Youth.*

[P86]
The mountain range called martial arts was vast and treacherous. Sometimes one had to cross a steep ravine or scale a sheer cliff.

[P87]
And Jeok Cheongang stood atop the peak at its farthest end.

[P88]
He had become something beyond his title of Fire King. So had one other person in this room.

[P89]
“Great Hero Jeok.”

[P90]
At Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s quiet call, the hot wind sweeping through the hall vanished.

[P91]
Jeok Cheongang drew in his aura at once and answered gruffly.

[P92]
“Did something happen?”

[P93]
“Hmm.”

[P94]
“All right, I know. That bastard was making too much noise, so I gave him a little scare.”

[P95]
No joke—if he scared Hwangbo Gun a second time, the man might wet himself. He was already back in his seat, white as a sheet.

[P96]
“Finally, some quiet,” Jeok Cheongang muttered.

[P97]
Mae Jonghak gave him a gently reproachful look, then turned to me.

[P98]
“Fire Dragon Pavilion Master.”

[P99]
“Yes.”

[P100]
“You have stood against Dark Heaven in Shanxi and Henan, and in Sichuan and Hubei.”

[P101]
*Gotten dragged into it* would have been more accurate, but I nodded.

[P102]
This was the Murim Alliance’s great conference hall. Sparring with Hwangbo Gun was one thing; discussing what came next was another.

[P103]
“That’s right.”

[P104]
“I expect few people know Dark Heaven as well as you. I would like to hear your opinion.”

[P105]
“I was only there when those things happened. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion knows more about the concrete evidence and what’s happening across the realm. I’ve already told them everything I know.”

[P106]
“I want to hear what you saw and experienced yourself. What the man who went through it all truly thinks.”

[P107]
*There we go.*

[P108]
What I’d said before was only a lead-in. Demurring once or twice was the polite thing to do, and if Mae Jonghak, speaking with the authority of the Murim Alliance Leader, pressed me for my opinion, it would carry that much more weight.

[P109]
*All right.*

[P110]
I took a small breath.

[P111]
Until now, I’d been sitting in the back seat. From here on, I was in the passenger seat.

[P112]
I couldn’t tell a driver setting out on an unfamiliar road at dawn, through thick fog and without navigation, everything I knew. But I could point out the speed bumps and warn him what lay ahead.

[P113]
*Including the ominous thought I haven’t been able to shake lately.*

[P114]
I sorted through my thoughts and raised my head. Everyone in the hall was looking at me.

[P115]
Dozens of pairs of eyes.

[P116]
These people could save hundreds, even thousands of lives in the war that had already begun. Or they could get them killed.

[P117]
How much heed they would pay to a kid barely past twenty, I couldn’t say.

[P118]
*It doesn’t matter. If we can win this war—if I can reduce the danger and the losses even a little—*

[P119]
I had to do what I could. Right now.

[P120]
Perhaps that was why my voice carried a weight it usually didn’t when I began to speak.

[P121]
“Dark Heaven…”

[P122]
* * *

[P123]
Two shichen later,[^1] everyone had left the great conference hall except three people.

[P124]
The chairs that had held dozens of people stood empty, but the silence that had settled over the room remained. Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho suspected those who had left the Alliance Leader’s Hall were just as quiet.

[P125]
*They had every reason to be.*

[P126]
Jin Taekyung’s words had been that shocking.

[P127]
Everyone knew Dark Heaven existed and understood that it was dangerous. No one, though, had warned of the coming crisis as forcefully as that young man.

[P128]
*Not even me.*

[P129]
The Hidden Shadow Pavilion gathered intelligence from across the realm and issued countless predictions. Hundreds of messenger pigeons arrived each day with information tied to their slender ankles, then flew off again before long.

[P130]
As its chief, Song Ho knew how dangerous Dark Heaven was.

[P131]
*But…*

[P132]
The thinking of the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s young master, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon whose actions had caused one upheaval after another, went far beyond anything Song Ho had expected.

[P133]
Where others spoke of danger, Jin Taekyung foretold disaster. When someone cited the Great Faction War as grounds for believing the Murim Alliance would win, he answered sharply.

[P134]
“Are we fighting the Demonic Cult? Our opponent is Dark Heaven. Dark Heaven.”

[P135]
“What Dark Heaven has shown us isn’t simply demonic martial arts. So what do I call it? Ah, this is driving me crazy. Fine. Let’s call it demonic martial arts for now.”

[P136]
“I don’t know why Dark Heaven has gone quiet, but we need to use this opening to strike back immediately. If we keep going like this, we’re finished. Everyone dies.”

[P137]
“Who said I was going too far? You, Family Head. Have you ever fought someone who came back to life even after all four limbs were crushed? Or fought an imugi? When you saw that monster half an hour ago, was all you could think about what to eat for dinner?”

[P138]
“We aren’t fighting ordinary people. Dark Heaven is one enormous monster, and before long, we may have to fight monsters like that one.”

[P139]
“I went a little too far. But this needs saying: we have to take every measure we can, right now. Especially if you’ve got a divine artifact at home that you guard like an ancestral shrine.”

[P140]
Song Ho suddenly furrowed his brow.

[P141]
The place where his prosthetic leg attached had begun to throb when Jin Taekyung started speaking. Now it burned.

[P142]
*It wasn’t like this even a year ago.*

[P143]
The pain had returned at some point and begun tormenting him in his old age, as though warning him this was no time to sit still.

[P144]
And today, that young man was here too.

[P145]
*It was as though he knew. As though he’d already experienced something and could foresee a truth hidden from me and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion—no, from everyone else.*

[P146]
Foresee? No. Song Ho corrected himself.

[P147]
*It was more like a prophecy.*

[P148]
The question was whether it truly was one.

[P149]
Could he trust the young man who, more than anyone else in the realm, had come into contact with Dark Heaven? How much of what he’d said was truth, and how much was exaggeration?

[P150]
“Believe him.”

[P151]
“Hm?”

[P152]
Song Ho looked up sharply. Jeok Cheongang, still in the hall, continued.

[P153]
“I said, believe him.”

[P154]
“Great Hero Jeok.”

[P155]
“I know what you’re going to say. But…”

[P156]
His tone softened.

[P157]
“The kid I know has never once been wrong.”

[P158]
“……!”

[P159]
Song Ho faltered at the absolute trust in those words.

[P160]
Then Mae Jonghak, the last of the three remaining in the hall, spoke.

[P161]
“There are certainties in this world that information alone cannot lead us to.”

[P162]
“Alliance Leader. Do you mean…?”

[P163]
“That’s right.”

[P164]
Mae Jonghak rose slowly from his seat.

[P165]
“Summon him. It’s time to give the Fire Dragon Pavilion its first mission.”

[P166]
[^1]: A shichen is a traditional time unit lasting approximately two hours.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
